speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia B (Christmas Disease).

The history of spontaneous hemarthrosis in a young male with a family history of similar joint issues, combined with normal uric acid and normal imaging (ruling out infection or crystals), strongly points to a hereditary bleeding disorder. While hemophilia A is more common, the specific family lineage described is consistent with Hemophilia B.
